chapter: New Orleans halls and street bands
title: St. Elizabeth Hall and lawn parties
summary: Questions about particular halls and lawn parties, including a yard where Armstrong sat in.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: What were some of those halls? Did you ever work at St. Elizabeth?
Yeah, sure. That's the hall I tried to call. That's up above the Poirier Avenue. That's the one I tried to call, St. Elizabeth.
Well, it was the St. Catharines. Did you ever work over here by Tulane on the church? I don't know the church. Is that St. Catharines Church?
Yeah, there's a hall there called St. Catharines. Right across from the church. Yeah, but I never did play there.
The fucking baby dog. Yeah, I never did play there.
What about the Million Willows? Did you ever hear that?
Well, that Million Willows. Million Willows.
The T. Thurden Willows. I think that's what it is. Yeah, Thurden Willows.
That's where the National Park was. The National Park.
Yeah, I mean we played there every Monday night, Sunday night. But what about Miss Cole's lawn parties?
I was just at Fing and Willows. Yeah, I played there a couple of times too. A little yard, you know? Yeah. I mean we played there every Monday night, Sunday night.
But what about Miss Cole's lawn parties?

That was just at Fing and Willows. Yeah, I played there a couple of times too. And used to have a little place right back of Perdita Street there. A little yard, you know? Yeah. Right there. Perdita and Satova, I think. It was a Franklin. One of them streets. But that's where Lewis used to get off the boat and come catch me playing there all the time to sit in and play with me.
Who ran that place? Was that?
Yeah, Toodle-um. Yeah. Just on that page.
